title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
title_zh: RoboJudge：多模态大模型作为具身视频生成的评判者

paragraphs.en: 总结：该文章提出RoboJudge-Bench评测多模态大模型评判具身视频生成的能力，并训练出与人类评分相关性最高的RoboJudge-9B模型。 Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.
paragraphs.zh: 总结：该文章提出RoboJudge-Bench评测多模态大模型评判具身视频生成的能力，并训练出与人类评分相关性最高的RoboJudge-9B模型。视频生成模型有望成为具身世界模型的基础，但前提是其生成的推演结果在物理上有效且忠实于任务指令。 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）日益被用于评判这些属性，但其在具身视频上与人类判断的一致性尚未得到系统性评估。 为填补这一空白，我们提出RoboJudge-Bench，一个用于评估多模态大语言模型作为具身视频生成评判者的基准。 该基准衡量两个基本维度——物理贴合性与指令一致性，涵盖来自8个源语料库和10个视频生成器的800个由人工标注的视频，涉及夹爪、人手和灵巧手。 实验揭示了现有评判模型与人类评分之间的对齐程度参差不齐：通用多模态大语言模型在物理贴合性上的一致性较低，而专为通用领域物理推理设计的专用视频评判模型也未必能一致地迁移到具身场景中。 基于这些发现，我们构建了RoboJudge-Train，其中包含12K个视频，带有25K个经人工核验的评分，以及针对物理贴合性和指令一致性的模型辅助推理说明。 我们在该数据集上先通过监督学习再通过强化学习对一个9B多模态大语言模型进行微调，得到RoboJudge-9B。 在RoboJudge-Bench上评估的各类模型评判者中，RoboJudge-9B取得了最高的总体一致性，皮尔逊相关系数达到0.719，相较我们评估中表现最佳的专有基线Gemini-3.7-Flash高出0.089，且该提升具有统计显著性。 在RoboJudge-Train上训练也在外部基准上带来了提升，包括VideoPhy2和Physion-Eval。 我们进一步将RoboJudge-9B用作下游评估器，依据物理贴合性和指令一致性对视频生成模型进行基准测试。
